subject: Post-demo: throughput / budget scope + continuous-batching assumptions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.ai>, salesops@acme.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: throughput / budget scope + continuous-batching assumptions

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap so we all have the same baseline and clear next steps. I’ve kept it short; see attached deck + scope workbook for the POC draft.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Target production ramp: initial 10–20M tokens/month, ramping to ~60M over 12 months.
- Monthly budget range: $8k–$50k initially (depends on ramp profile).
- Unit economics target: ~USD 800 / 1M tokens for generation traffic (customer target range: 600–1000), embeddings negotiated separately.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn generation (streaming acceptable, client-side assembly ok).

Continuous batching & concurrency assumptions we discussed:
- Workload shape: mostly customer-facing generation via short prompts (avg prompt+response ~180 tokens), 10% long-form (>1k tokens) spikes.
- Baseline QPS: 35–55 sustained, peak bursts to ~120 qps for short windows.
- Expected concurrency for inferencing: 20–50 concurrent active requests (depends on client-side retry/backoff).
- Continuous batching expectations: we’ll leave batching window at 40–80ms for low-latency paths, with continuous prefix caching for repeat traffic. That maps to effective per-GPU throughput gains of ~2.0–2.8x vs naive single-request serving (rough estimate for planning).

Open questions / asks from Acme (action items):
1) Sophie: confirm the expected monthly token distribution (short vs long requests) and any hourly calendarization (are spikes regional/time-of-day sensitive?).
2) Acme ops: sign off on the POC scope workbook (attached) + confirm required security docs (SOC2 evidence) we should include.
3) Redwood: provide a two-week POC quote (estimated commit + telemetry plan) and a small test key for sandbox.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today: share POC workbook + draft MPA (attached).
- EOD Friday: Acme to return the token distribution sample and security checklist.
- Mon next week: kickoff call to provision test capacity.

If any of this needs to be corrected, flag here and I’ll update the doc.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope.xlsx (worksheet: token_profile), proposed-mpa.pdf (draft terms)

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.ai>

Cc: salesops@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput / budget scope + continuous-batching assumptions

Thanks Mina — useful recap. A few clarifications from my side:
- Monthly tokens: our initial plan is closer to 12–18M tokens/month in month 1–3, targeting 40–60M by month 12 if engagement metrics look good.
- Distribution: ~85% short interactions (<=200 tokens total), ~10% medium (200–1k), ~5% long (>1k).
- Spikes: yes — we have predictable spikes aligned with product marketing pushes (approx 2–3 days/month when traffic doubles). Spikes are mostly between 10:00–18:00 PT.
- Budget: the $8k–$50k range looks right for now; priority is keeping unit $/1M below $900. Embeddings are a separate line item; we’ll estimate embedding volume after the POC.

We can get the token sample exported from our metrics team by Friday. SOC2 docs: please share the checklist you need; we have an internal secure folder for documents.

Sophie
Sophie Turner
Head of Platform, AcmeAI
Sophie.Turner@acme.ai

Portable note — quick operational guidance while we wait for the token export:
- Default concurrency planning: size the POC for 50 concurrent requests to match the mid-case. That gives headroom for 2x burst behavior.
- Batching window recommendation: start conservative at 60ms for the low-latency route; we can widen to 120ms for the bulk path if Acme can accept 50–100ms additional latency during batch consolidation.
- Cost sensitivity: changing batching windows has an outsized impact on effective $/1M. I’ll include two sensitivity slices in Monica’s estimate (60ms vs 120ms).

Mina / Monica — once you have the workbook updated, I’ll pull the POC pricing code and a short runbook for provisioning dedicated test capacity. Sophie — if April 29 works, we’ll schedule the kickoff and reserve a small slab.

-Markus
